audit_question: Do the eleven representative decks provide enough archetype and mechanic diversity for HSConfig's current lean pre-run CustomConfig purpose, while keeping fixture stages, strongness visibility, expected runtime surfaces, and known coverage limits explicit and actionable?
confirmed_facts: HSConfig defines itself as a pre-run-only deck-to-CustomConfig compiler and explicitly excludes replay parsing, winrate inspection, runtime log analysis, candidate promotion, and post-run tuning from its normal purpose.

The operator guide names docs/operator/archetype-fixture-matrix.json as the representative 11-deck proof set and says the normal next action is to close existing source_informed rows before adding more decks.
The matrix contains exactly 11 enforced rows: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, Kingslayer, Boarlock, and PirateDH.
The current stage split is 4 core_source_backed_fixture decks and 7 source_informed_valid_fixture decks.

The four core strong control fixtures are ShadowPriest, PirateRogue, BigShaman, and MechPala. The seven breadth fixtures are CtAPaladin, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, Kingslayer, Boarlock, and PirateDH.
Across the 11 rows, the matrix covers 11 distinct archetype buckets, 31 distinct primary mechanic tags, and 22 distinct decision families.
All 11 rows expect GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, and deck-local <CARDID>.json files. Only Boarlock currently expects Combo.json, which keeps exact combo support visible but intentionally narrow.
Strongness visibility is explicit for every row through current_stage, first_strongness_gap, and operator_action, and tests enforce the expected gap label for each deck.

The closure document records the current blocker snapshot as 0 guide gaps, 0 runtime-surface gaps, and 0 mechanic-lowering gaps for ShadowPriest, PirateRogue, BigShaman, and MechPala, while the seven source_informed decks still expose deck-specific guide-depth or lowering work.

Known limits are documented per row. Repeated limits include missing reactive control coverage, incomplete discover-chain coverage, narrow exact-combo coverage, and only one single_combo_fixture_only row.

Fresh repo verification passed on 2026-07-08: python -m pytest tests/test_archetype_fixture_matrix.py tests/test_archetype_source_fixtures.py tests/test_archetype_fixture_e2e.py tests/test_matrix_visibility.py tests/test_matrix_closure.py -q returned 52 passed in 11.89s.
strengths: The 11-deck matrix is broad enough for HSConfig's current purpose because it spans fast face pressure, recruit board flood, pirate tempo, big-cheat recruit, discard, token snowball, hero-power spell generation, mech scaling, weapon sequencing, combo-resource setup, and hero-attack pressure without turning the repo into a large template catalog.

Breadth is operational, not aspirational: each matrix row has a matching source_documents_<deck>_strong.json fixture and passes through current tests that build source bundles or prepare valid packages.
The matrix keeps scope discipline. It proves pre-game package generation breadth instead of drifting into HSTuner or runtime-tuning concerns.
Fixture-stage visibility is strong. Operators can see which rows are already core controls, which rows still need closure, and what the first missing strongness link is for each deck.

Expected runtime surfaces are intentionally lean and consistent. GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, and per-card CardID files are universal, while Combo.json appears only where the repo has an explicit exact-sequence case.
gaps_or_risks: Breadth is adequate for current pre-run auditing, but it is not exhaustive. Seven of the eleven rows are still source_informed_valid_fixture rather than source_backed_strong.

Reactive control remains the clearest structural blind spot. Seven rows explicitly record does_not_cover_reactive_control, so the matrix is weaker on long attrition, removal sequencing, and defensive stabilization than on proactive tempo and board plans.
Discover-heavy and choice-heavy behavior is still underrepresented at the deck-matrix level. Three rows explicitly record does_not_cover_discover_chains.
Exact combo breadth is intentionally narrow. Boarlock is the only row that expects Combo.json, and its known limit is single_combo_fixture_only.
Some families overlap by design, which is good for a lean matrix but means adding more pirate, weapon, or board-centric decks would likely increase maintenance more than coverage.
The matrix should not be read as proof of gameplay optimality or post-run tuning quality. It is a coverage and operability proof set for HSConfig's pre-run compiler.
eleven_deck_implications: For HSConfig's current purpose, the answer is yes with an important boundary: the eleven decks are diverse enough to act as the representative proof matrix for lean pre-run package generation, but they are not diverse enough to claim exhaustive mechanic closure.
The current matrix already captures the main proactive decision families HSConfig needs to compile today, so the immediate priority is not widening the deck list.

The most useful work is to promote the seven source_informed_valid_fixture rows by closing their first strongness gaps: recruit and aura runtime surfaces for CtAPaladin, discard and hand mutation for Discolock, token board buffing for TreantDruid, hero-power spell generation for ImbueMage, weapon sequencing for Kingslayer, exact combo sequencing for Boarlock, and hero-attack runtime surfaces for PirateDH.
If a future audit keeps failing on a family the matrix does not represent well, the best next candidate is a reactive control or discover-heavy deck rather than another proactive tempo deck.
Because the matrix already encodes decision_families_proven and known_coverage_limits per row, it is suitable for ongoing fixture-breadth auditing without adding more decks immediately.
recommendation: Keep the current eleven-deck matrix as HSConfig's default fixture-breadth boundary. Treat it as sufficient for present pre-run operability audits, but not as full mechanic closure. Do not expand the deck set now. First close the seven existing source_informed_valid_fixture rows until more of the matrix reaches SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG. Add one new representative deck only if repeated audits show a real missing family that none of the current eleven can exercise, with reactive control or discover-heavy behavior as the strongest next candidate.
